title: Work In Progress: Towards Adaptive RF Fingerprint-based Authentication of IIoT devices
objective: Address security vulnerabilities in IIoT by enabling flexible and accurate authentication through adaptive RF fingerprinting.
methodology: AI-driven adaptive Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) at the PHY layer, combined with Software-Defined Radio (SDR) gateways and Edge/Cloud computing for feature extraction and authentication.
performance: High accuracy in device authentication over challenging RF environments through adaptive feature extraction and SDR tuning.
limitations: Dependence on SDR processing power and SNR, limited by current feature extraction methods and lack of standardized protocols.

title: DeepCRF: Deep Learning-Enhanced CSI-Based RF Fingerprinting for Channel-Resilient WiFi Device Identification
objective: To address limitations of prior signal space-based methods in non-line-of-sight scenarios and improve WiFi device identification under varying channel conditions.
methodology: CNN with model-inspired data augmentation, supervised contrastive learning, and decision fusion for enhanced generalization and noise resilience in CSI-based fingerprinting.
dataset: 19 COTS WiFi NICs with CSI measurements across diverse channel conditions, including real-world unseen scenarios.
performance: Achieves 99.53% average identification accuracy using 4 CSI measurements per procedure across 19 COTS devices in real-world scenarios (metrics: Accuracy, F1 Score, AUC-ROC).
limitations: Reliance on CSI measurements and potential generalization challenges in highly dynamic environments.

title: Federated Radio Frequency Fingerprint Identification Powered by Unsupervised Contrastive Learning
objective: Address data scarcity challenges in RFFI systems by proposing a federated learning framework with unsupervised contrastive learning for IoT networks.
methodology: Three-stage federated RFFI protocol: federated pre-training, client fine-tuning, and identification using unsupervised contrastive learning for feature extraction.
dataset: 60 commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) LoRa transmitters and 6 software-defined radio (SDR) receivers.
performance: Identification accuracy improved from 63% to 95%; robustness to receiver hardware variations and location changes achieved.
limitations: Previous federated RFFI systems lack trainability, scalability, and security due to reliance on labeled data and model aggregation challenges.

title: RF eigenﬁngerprints, an Efﬁcient RF Fingerprinting Method in IoT Context
objective: Address limitations of cryptographic methods in IoT by proposing RF eigenﬁngerprints for non-cryptographic authentication using device impairments.
methodology: Adapts eigenfaces approach with singular value decomposition (SVD) and Ljung–Box test for feature selection, combined with statistical models for authentication. Includes simulation, real-world experiments, and FPGA implementation.
dataset: Extended Yale Face database B for eigenfaces; novel baseband model for emitter impairments (I/Q offset, imbalance, PA nonlinearity).
performance: Demonstrates scalability, low computational complexity, high explainability, and successful validation through simulation, real-world experiments, and FPGA implementation.
limitations: Depends on preamble-based signal processing and assumes controlled hardware variability.

title: NOT MENTIONED
objective: To address the challenge of distinguishing same-model devices in RF fingerprinting by creating a large-scale homogeneous dataset and a reproducible framework, overcoming limitations of existing datasets with small scale and heterogeneous models.
methodology: Developed a large-scale dataset with 123 same-model IEEE 802.11g devices, 35.42 million raw I/Q samples, and 1.85 million RF features. Created a reproducible framework with data collection, feature extraction, and benchmark evaluation modules.
dataset: Two CSV datasets: (1) RFFI-IQ_only-wifi-802.11g-2.4G-123-m5stack (MAC addresses and preamble samples) and (2) RFFI-kf_feature-IQ-wifi-802.11g-2.4G-123-m5stack (multi-dimensional RF features including CFO, phase error, magnitude error, and fractal dimension).
performance: Random Forest-based algorithm achieved 89.06% identification accuracy. Features included CFO correction, phase error, magnitude error, and fractal dimension. Evaluation metrics: identification accuracy, feature extraction completeness, and reproducibility of results.
limitations: Focus on same-model devices limits generalizability to heterogeneous scenarios. Requires additional processing for RF feature extraction.
